sections.h2: Selling a house fast in Lakewood
sections.html:
In Lakewood you may hire an agent, sell it yourself or take a cash offer for the house as it stands. What the house is and how it is used should pick the route. An empty, tidy house can go on the market. One with tenants, postponed repairs or an estate behind it usually moves quicker through a direct sale.

Owners live in fewer than half of Lakewood homes, 47.5 percent to be exact. Rent runs a midpoint of $1,525 a month, and owner-occupied homes have a median value of $461,200. A city registration and inspection program for rentals, described below, affects how a rented house sells.

Lakewood was incorporated on February 28, 1996 and became the second largest city in Pierce County at once. Joint Base Lewis-McChord, a military installation with about 55,000 employees, sits beside the city, and the local economy is closely tied to it. State Route 512 ends where it meets Interstate 5 in Lakewood, and the Lakewood Sounder station runs commuter trains north through Tacoma to Seattle. The mean commute is 29.3 minutes.

sections.h2: How the Rental Housing Safety Program affects a sale
sections.html:
The city's Rental Housing Safety Program requires owners of rental property to register every year, and registered properties are inspected once every five years. An initial inspection may be done by a city inspector or by a qualified private inspector, and every re-inspection is done by the city. Inspectors look at structural integrity, weather exposure, plumbing and sanitation, heat and water, ventilation, electrical wiring, exits, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors.

An owner who fails to register can face penalties under the city's fee schedule and the Lakewood Municipal Code, and a rental business license can be revoked. A buyer of a rented house will ask for registration and inspection records, so gather them before you list. Exemptions under LMC 5.60.025 include:

  • Units occupied by the owner, or by the owner's parent or child.
  • Mobile and manufactured homes, shelters and transitional housing.
  • Condominiums and townhouses in multi-unit structures under multiple ownership, unless one owner holds them.
  • Units built in the past 10 years with a certificate of occupancy and no code violations.

Renting rooms in a home you live in does not require registration, but moving out and renting the whole house does. Contact the program at 253-512-2261 or rentals@cityoflakewood.us.

Rentals of under 30 days are allowed in most zones. The city excludes Commercial 1 to 3, the Industrial Business Park, Industrial 1 and 2, Public and Semi-Public Institutional and Open Space Recreation 1 and 2. A short-term rental must register with the Rental Housing Safety Program, hold a business license, renew annually and be inspected every five years, with a free first inspection. The city handles the permit as a Type II administrative decision. Check your zoning before you promise a buyer short-term rental income.

Several providers share the city's services, so it helps to list them when you transfer utility accounts to a buyer:

  • Clover Park School District runs most public schools, with parts of Lakewood in the Steilacoom Historical and Tacoma districts.
  • Electricity comes from Lakeview Light and Power on the east side, Tacoma Power on the north side and Puget Sound Energy on the west side, which is also the only natural gas provider.
  • The Lakewood Water District supplies tap water.
  • Pierce County Public Works and Utilities maintains sanitary sewer, and the city manages stormwater.
  • West Pierce Fire and Rescue covers the city.

List the providers for your address in the sale file so the buyer knows whom to call on day one.

sections.h2: When Pierce County property taxes are due
sections.html:
Statements arrive in February. A bill over $50 can be paid in two installments, April 30 and October 31, while $50 or less must be paid in full on April 30. If a payment envelope is postmarked before the statutory deadline, interest and penalty are waived. Check your statement for the exact amounts due.

Pay online or at the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, Tacoma, which also has a drop box. Foreclosure avoidance payments go by cashier's check to that office. For status, call the Assessor-Treasurer hotline at (253) 798-6111. Mortgage companies follow the same payment rules as the owner.

sections.h2: What a Lakewood seller owes and discloses at closing
sections.html:
The seller normally covers the state real estate excise tax, payable on the sale date, with a city local tax on top. Under RCW 82.45.060 the state rate climbs in steps from 1.1 percent on the first slice, and the thresholds change January 1, 2027. Your escrow officer can give you the exact figure for your price, state and local together.

The disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 asks about the sewer connection, roof leaks and environmental items. A buyer who receives it may rescind within three business days, unless the contract says differently.

Once you accept an offer, escrow orders a title search and requests your lender's payoff. The excise tax, the prorated property tax and other costs are added up on the settlement statement. For a rented house, the registration certificate and inspection results should be in the file by then. If the inspection is not current, ask the program whether a private inspector or a city inspector should do it, because the choice can affect timing.

A cash buyer often skips the appraisal and loan committee, so these steps can finish sooner. Whatever route you pick, compare offers by what you take home after the payoff, taxes and any repairs, and confirm your last property tax payment has posted before closing day.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell a rented Lakewood house
sections.html:
With a tenant in place, begin with documents. Find your current registration certificate and inspection results, and call 253-512-2261 to ask if an exemption covers your unit. Add the lease and rent records so a buyer can see exactly what comes with the property.

An investor keeping the tenant cares about those records and the next inspection date. A buyer moving in cares about condition and about when the unit can be emptied. A tidy file speeds talks in both cases. Before agreeing to a closing date, ask a Washington attorney how your lease and notice duties apply.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my Lakewood rental before selling?
faqs.a: Each year the house is rented, unless an exemption applies. Buyers ask for the certificate and inspection history, so register and inspect first if you have not.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lakewood house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Expect a buyer who keeps the tenant to review the city's registration and inspection records. A Washington attorney can explain your lease and notice duties.

faqs.q: When are Pierce County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments, April 30 and October 31, except that $50 or less is due in full April 30. April 30, 2027 is the next first-half date.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Lakewood?
faqs.a: Yes, in most zones, with a business license, registration in the Rental Housing Safety Program and a permit. Commercial 1 to 3 and several industrial and open space zones are excluded.

faqs.q: Who pays excise tax when a Lakewood house sells?
faqs.a: Usually the seller, payable to the county treasurer on the sale date. Unpaid tax accrues interest starting that day.
